These give the surrounding section, ch. 1 §1.2 'Accento': p.32 'Per quanto…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Neapolitan word stress is lexically determined and not predictable from the segmental string (final, penultimate and antepenultimate stress all occur, with minimal pairs such as ['kommə] vs [kom'mɔ], [ka'pillə] vs [kapil'lo]); it is confined to the last three syllables: when enclitics would push stress further left than the antepenult, stress is shifted rightward onto the penultimate syllable of the verb+clitic group, with gemination of the following consonant (làssa+me+ne > lassamènne). Capozzoli 1889:214 §145 states the same enclitic rule ('Queste voci diventano bisdrucciole, debbono rendersi piane, raddoppiando l'ultima consonante').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing on secondary stress in the accessible snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitic clusters trigger obligatory stress shift to the penult (Ledgeway p.34, p.89, p.314; Capozzoli 1889:214-215); Ledgeway p.35 notes that in old texts 3rd-person accusative clitics behaved differently (snippet truncated).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress ('accento primario/principale della parola'); the enclitic shift concerns the verb + clitic group (phonological word). Citation forms in IPA with final unstressed vowels reduced to [ə].
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Ledgeway 2009) describes Neapolitan proper, the dialect of the city of Naples, which is the flagship variety of Glottolog's language-level code neap1235 'Continental Southern Italian' (ISO 639-3 nap); that code also subsumes Abruzzese, Molisano, northern Pugliese (e.g. Barese) and northern Lucanian dialects, some of which have their own descriptions in the Glottolog list (Savini 1881 Teramano was checked here and is silent on stress). Glottolog has a dialect-level entry for Neapolitan under neap1235; Capozzoli 1889 likewise describes (literary) Neapolitan of Naples.

new_statements.quote: Whenever phonetic detail is irrelevant (especially in §§16.3-4), forms will be cited in a broadly Italian-based orthography where: (i) ch/gh = [k]/[g] (otherwise h = Ø), ... (ii) all orthographically double consonants are realized long; (iii) unless otherwise indicated (by an acute accent whenever vowel quality is irrelevant), stress is paroxytonic. ... It should also be noted that in most upper southern Italian dialects unstressed (and especially front) vowels are typically realized as schwa (cf. §16.2.1.2), especially word-finally (e.g., Nap. càmmara/-e ['kammərə] 'bedroom/-s', surdato/-e [sur'datə] 'soldier/-s', vénnere ['vennərə] 'sell.INF').

(ii) all orthographically double consonants are realized long; (iii) unless otherwise indicated (by an acute accent whenever vowel quality is irrelevant), stress is paroxytonic.' and '.. in most upper southern Italian dialects unstressed (and especially front) vowels are typically realized as schwa (cf. §16.2.1.2), especially word-finally (e.g., Nap. càmma…
new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing Ledgeway 2009 statement (primary stress lexically unpredictable, with a 'sensibile preferenza generale per l'accentuazione parossitona' and a three-syllable window): the 2016 chapter states the paroxytone default explicitly as its transcription convention and adds morphological detail (proparoxytone vs paroxytone infinitive classes, accentual distinction veré/vénnere, stressed enclitics cross-ref). It does not state a phonological rule of its own and says nothing on the three-syllable window or secondary stress. The listed open_url (the Harvard library catalogue record) was the wrong item: its docid resolves to Ledgeway 2023, 'Differential object marking in the…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The chapter gives no phonological account of word stress; its only general statement is a transcription convention: cited dialect forms are paroxytone (penultimate stress) unless an acute accent marks another position. Stress is thus treated as lexically variable with penultimate placement as the unmarked default, and the chapter itself cites many marked forms (proparoxytone Nap. càmmara, vénnere, móvere, pártere; oxytone Nap. partí, veré).
new_statements.exceptions: Forms with non-penultimate stress are marked orthographically (acute accent). p. 259: in the upper south and northern Calabria the class-2 infinitive 'converges on the original third conjugation proparoxytonic type' (Nap./Cos. móvere/vénnere/pártere), 'although in some original fourth conjugation infinitives the paroxytonic variant still optionally survives (e.g., Nap. partí)'; in southern Calabrian and Sicilian the infinitive 'oscillates between the original third/fourth pro-/paroxytonic types (cádiri/cadíri..)'. p. 258: 'Except in the infinitive where in some dialects of the upper south the Latin second/third conjugations are still accentually distinguished (e.g., UIDÉRE/UÉNDERE > Nap. veré/vénnere)'; footnote: 'For discussion of stressed enclitics in southern dialects, see §45.3.1.' p. 260: the verb 'be' 'presents rhizotonic stress throughout the paradigm' (Tarantino, Sicilian forms).
new_statements.identity_note: Ledgeway 2016 is a survey of all dialects of southern Italy (upper south: Campania incl. Neapolitan, Abruzzo, Molise, Puglia, Basilicata, northern Calabria; extreme south: Sicily, southern Calabria, Salento). Its stress convention (p. 246 fn. 1) is stated for all cited dialect forms, not for Neapolitan specifically, though its illustrative examples on that page are Neapolitan (càmmara, surdato, vénnere). The the Harvard library catalogue open_url pointed to a different work (Ledgeway 2023, Caplletra 74, on differential object marking).

sources.citation: Capozzoli, Raffaele. 1889. Grammatica del dialetto napoletano. Napoli: Luigi Chiurazzi. 224 pp. (§145, pp. 214-215)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No general stress-placement rule (orthoepy/orthography chapter only recommends writing the accent on the tonic vowel). §145 p.214: when enclitics lo, la, le, me, te, se, ne, ve are added to verb forms, forms that would become 'bisdrucciole' (pre-antepenultimate stress) 'debbono rendersi piane, raddoppiando l'ultima consonante' (must become paroxytone, doubling the last consonant): not avìssemelo, tòrnamelo but avissemèllo, tornamèllo, lassamènne etc. -- i.e. an explicit ban on stress further left than the antepenult.
